## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
`save_report` swallows every `OSError` and still prints a success message and returns 0, so a failed save is reported as successful. This must be fixed before merge, and the test for an unavailable destination needs to assert the failure.

## Changes
The pull request adds `save_report` to `app/reports.py`, which writes the rendered report and prints where it was saved. It also adds `cleanup_report`, which deletes a temporary report and ignores one that is already gone. New tests in `tests/test_reports.py` cover both functions.

## Critical
- app/reports.py:8 — silent-failure — Propagate or signal save failures instead of passing — When the destination directory is missing or not writable, `except OSError: pass` discards the error. Execution then continues to `print(f"Report saved to {path}")` and `return 0`, so the caller gets a success message and status for a file that was never written. — Users and calling scripts believe the report was saved when it was not, and they get no error to act on. — Fix: Let the `OSError` propagate, or print an error naming `path` and the OS reason and return a nonzero status without printing the success message.

## Important
- tests/test_reports.py:14 — tests — Assert the outcome in the unavailable-destination test — `test_save_with_unavailable_destination` calls `save_report` on `tmp_path / "missing" / "report.txt"` and asserts nothing. It passes whether the function raises, returns nonzero, or falsely reports success. — The failed-save path has no regression protection, so the false-success defect passes the suite unnoticed.
